text.name: TextDesc2
text.text: The Sega AI Computer was a Japanese educational home computer introduced by Sega in 1986. Based on the architecture of the SG-1000 and SC-3000 computer, it was designed as a low-cost learning system aimed at children and students. The machine featured a Zilog Z80A processor, 64 KB of RAM, a full keyboard, cartridge support, and cassette storage for saving programs and educational software. It remained compatible with much of Sega's existing SC-3000 software and hardware while emphasizing programming and computer literacy through BASIC and educational titles. Although released during the transition to more powerful 16-bit home computers, the Sega AI Computer provided an affordable introduction to computing and is remembered as the final evolution of Sega's 8-bit computer line before the company shifted its focus entirely to dedicated video game consoles.
